span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Natural selection coadapts polygene complexes only within a population, so chromosomes brought together from populations that never interbreed have not been mutually adjusted and their heterozygotes lack heterosis.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Heterosis arises from interaction between polygene complexes carried by differently arranged chromosomes, which the inversions protect from being broken up by crossing over in the heterozygote.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A second, distinct kind of heterosis arises when deleterious recessive mutants accumulated in the population are sheltered by their normal dominant alleles in the heterozygote.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Viability and adaptive value diverge because larval survival is only one of several components (adult longevity, fecundity, sexual activity) that jointly determine net fitness.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The cages were not run long enough for the inferior chromosome type to be eliminated, so the predicted outcome was not observed to completion.
span.note: what this limits: the elimination prediction specifically: THE CH CHROMOSOMES WERE RARE IN CAGES NOS. 48 AND 49, BUT MUCH LONGER OBSERVATION WOULD BE NEEDED TO SEE THEM ELIMINATED COMPLETELY
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In the California-Mexico cage No. 55 the viability differences among genotypes did not reach conventional significance.
span.note: what this limits: the viability comparison in cage No. 55: THE DIFFERENCES ARE, HOWEVER, MOSTLY BELOW THE CONVENTIONAL LEVEL OF STATISTICAL SIGNIFICANCE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper opens its discussion by saying the term names several scarcely related phenomena that the field treats as one.
span.note: what this limits: any result reported as heterosis or hybrid vigor: the paper states these terms Quotation withheld, so two such results need not be about the same thing
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Fitness measured at one developmental stage can point the opposite way from fitness overall, and the paper gives its own case.
span.note: what this limits: a fitness or survival figure from a single developmental stage: adaptive value is stated not to be proportional to survival value at all stages, and here some types with higher egg-to-adult mortality were nevertheless adaptively superior
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The effect is a property of chromosomes that evolved together, so the same gene-arrangement label does not carry the same behaviour between localities.
span.note: what this limits: a heterosis result carried from one population to another: polygene complexes from geographically distant localities have not undergone coadaptation, so the same chromosomal type does not behave the same way in a different population
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: inversion heterozygotes compared against inversion homozygotes, with the paper noting that the heterozygotes were also heterozygous for geographical gene complexes
span.note: eliminates: very little on its own - and the paper says so, which is why this is worth recording: it names the confound its own comparison does not remove
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Inversion heterozygotes built from two third chromosomes of the same population show heterosis, but heterozygotes built from chromosomes of geographically remote populations generally do not.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In every geographically mixed cage one homozygote was sharply less viable than the heterozygote (quotients 0.17 to 0.76) while another homozygote was more viable than it, so the heterozygote was intermediate rather than superior.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: When the design was inverted so that the homozygotes carried chromosomes of mixed geographic origin and the heterozygotes carried same-population chromosomes, heterosis reappeared, showing it depends on the origin of the third chromosomes rather than on the genetic background.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Egg-to-adult viability and adaptive value can point in opposite directions: in cages 46 and 47 the adaptive values were ST/AR > ST/ST > AR/AR, the reverse of the measured viability order.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In the hybrid cages one chromosome type steadily displaced the other instead of settling at an equilibrium; Arrowhead of Mather origin rose from 50 to 91 percent while Chiricahua of Pinon origin fell to 9 percent over about 13 months.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: With chromosomes from California and Mexico combined, the Pinon Arrowhead homozygote was significantly more viable than the heterozygote and the Mexican Chiricahua homozygote was at least equal to it, so the heterozygote was inferior to both homozygotes.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: A genotype's net fitness is not proportional to its survival at every developmental stage; types with higher egg-to-adult mortality nevertheless proved adaptively superior in the cages.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
